data: {"type":"response.reasoning_summary_text.done","item_id":"rs_5fba844320f14a88b3e752dfa57fba12","output_index":0,"sequence_number":202,"summary_index":0,"text":"I see, so the internal model is as follows: `ConversationItem::System` (system instructions) and `User` items with `SyntheticReason::SystemReminder`. On the responses wire, `System` gets mapped to `role: system` (via `conversation_item_to_input_items`). But E2 says "developer" item — on the Responses API wire, the "system" role gets sent as "developer". Let me check what role `rs::Role::System` serializes to. Actually, the role in the responses API is "developer", and `rs::Role` might have a Developer variant. Let me check the rs types.

Now, the E2 bug: "A mid-prefix item reordering bug on the harness responses wire: a 'developer' item and `<system-reminder>` user item permanently swap their relative order once mid-session." So there's a "developer" item (probably an AGENTS.md / harness-injected instruction item) and a system-reminder user item, and after some event mid-session, the two end up in the opposite relative order compared to the earlier turns. Since the responses input is a replay of the entire history in item order, the cached prefix is pinned at the swap point: everything before the swap point stays cached (about 10.3k tokens frozen in the E2 case), and from the swap point onward gets re-written on every turn (113–1,004 cache-write tokens per turn).

Where is this happening? Probably in `xai-chat-state` (the actor), where items are appended: system-reminder user items get pushed via `push_user_message`, and there might be a "developer" item that gets (re-)injected or re-ordered somewhere — for example, on session rebuild / resume, or when the harness injects an "active agent state" developer item every turn, or on model switch (MAV2 rebuild), etc.

Let me check xai-chat-state's actor/state.rs and search for places where items get re-ordered / inserted. Search for "insert" / "reorder" / "position" within chat-state. Also, let me grep for "developer" within the shell to find the injection of developer items.
","model":"qwen3.8-27b"}
